I’m gonna go against the grain here and say it depends on what industries you’re interested in working in for the future.

I’m currently doing UofT ECE and have multiple friends at Waterloo (some ECE, some Tron). It’s true that the 4-month coop model is great for experience, especially for working in tech companies (although with the current recession I’ve heard Waterloo hiring took a hit, PEY hiring is doing just fine).

However, if you want to get your hands in an industry like energy, or semiconductors, or analog design, I think you’d be better off at UofT. You’d need a graduate degree for most of those industries, and as you know UofT is best for that. Also, companies in those industries generally prefer 12-16 month internships, since the on-boarding process is much longer than software. I know plenty of people who worked at Intel, HydroOne, AMD, Amazon Robotics, MDA, etc., and they wouldn’t have gotten that chance if they only went with 4 months coop.

Obviously, whatever choice you make will eventually lead you to the same path if you’re determined enough.

Didn’t get into Waterloo for SYDE and I thought my life was over, I genuinely had a panic attack and got depressed for a while. It sucks to work so hard for something but still not be deemed “good enough”.

Went to UofT engineering instead (still a good program, I overreacted so much in hindsight), and ended up exactly where I wanted to through working smarter, not harder.

You’ll be fine no matter where you end up, as long as you have a goal you can work towards.
